messages:
Andre (eng-platform): Heads-up — we need to sync on a small set of "customer-slice" metrics for the Console rollout. Goal: one page per customer showing isolation signals + quota windows.
Maya (eng-runtime): +1. What exact runtime signals are you expecting?
Andre (eng-platform): p95 latency, per-model kv-cache hit%, live batching queue depth, token/sec per org, model-fallback count. Also a compact recent-history sparkline for each.
Lucy (eng-infra): From infra we can add GPU_utilization{host}, avg_inflight_requests, connection_count_org. Question: do we want raw per-request traces or just aggregates? privacy matters.
Sam (product): Aggregates only for the public Console. For customers with enterprise consent we can show request-level sampling, but default must be scrubbed.
Jordan (eng-sre): For noisy-customer detection we need: sustained token/sec > X, burst_count over window, increasing KV cache evictions, and error-rate spikes. Can we agree on rule names/labels so Alerting can consume them?
Andre (eng-platform): Yes — let's pick canonical metric names that both runtime and infra emit. Proposal:
```
redwood.runtime.latency.p95{org_id, model}
redwood.runtime.kv_cache.hit_rate{org_id, model}
redwood.runtime.batching.queue_depth{org_id, route}
redwood.runtime.requests.tokens_per_sec{org_id}
redwood.runtime.fallbacks.count{org_id, fallback_model}
redwood.infra.gpu.utilization{host, pool}
redwood.infra.inflight.count{org_id}
redwood.infra.cache.evictions{org_id, cache_name}
```
Maya (eng-runtime): Fine with those names. A couple notes: emitting org_id on high-cardinality infra metrics will be expensive — we should instead emit org_id-tagged aggregates at a minute resolution and host-scoped metrics without org.
Lucy (eng-infra): Agreed — we'll emit host-level GPU metrics normally, and an aggregated org slice every 60s for billing/Console. Also will include a sample_id label when we emit request-sampled traces.
Sam (product): UX ask: Console needs a compact "isolation score" 0-100 per customer derived from a rule set. It should be a single number with tooltip listing contributing signals.
Jordan (eng-sre): We can compute the score in the metrics pipeline if we standardize the rule inputs. Eg: score = clamp(0,100, base + 20*burst_count_flag + 30*cache_eviction_rate). We'll publish the formula as part of the rollout.
Andre (eng-platform): Permissions: only org admins + Redwood support staff with just-in-time access can view detailed traces. Console will show aggregates to normal users. Product: can you wire the entitlement UI?
Sam (product): Yep — we'll add a per-customer toggle for "detailed telemetry access" and an audit log entry.
Maya (eng-runtime): For noisy-customer auto-mitigation: if score > 80, runtime should reduce batching window for that org and route to lower-cost variant if available. Need a safe fallback policy and cooldown to avoid oscillation.
Lucy (eng-infra): Also suggest a soft quota throttle at the edge (reject 429) with explanatory code so SDKs can fallback gracefully.
Jordan (eng-sre): Add an emergency bypass for support-staff to temporarily raise quota for legit sustained spikes after manual verification. Audit all bypasses.
Andre (eng-platform): Okay action items: 1) Teams agree on metric names & cardinality limits (runtime + infra) — Maya/Lucy by EOD Thursday. 2) Sam to prototype isolation score UI and entitlement flow by next week. 3) Jordan to draft alert rules (noisy-customer detection) and mitigation playbook. 4) I will update Console schema and telemetry docs.
metrics-bot: deployed metrics-change: redwood.runtime.kv_cache.hit_rate new label: model (2026-08-12T15:02:00Z).
Maya (eng-runtime): Noted. We'll drop model label on high-cardinality host metrics and only emit model on aggregated streams.
Lucy (eng-infra): I'll post the ingestion budget limits — suggest 10 label cardinality per org for minute-aggregates.
Sam (product): Thx — small ask: can the isolation score be exportable as CSV for customer support?
Andre (eng-platform): Yes, exportable and downloadable for 30 days.
Jordan (eng-sre): One more: include model-version in fallback/count metrics so we can see if a variant rollout caused noise.
Maya (eng-runtime): Will add model_version label to redwood.runtime.fallbacks.count (low-res aggregate).
Andre (eng-platform): Great. If nobody objects I'll convert this thread into a short doc and tracker ticket. Thanks all :thumbsup:
